output.program:
domain(person,[ramon]).

% If Ramon plays chess, then he either anticipates outcomes or studies games, but not both.
axiom(s1,rule([plays_chess(ramon)],xor(anticipates_outcomes(ramon),studies_games(ramon)))).

% Ramon analyzes situations.
axiom(s2,analyzes_situations(ramon)).

% If Ramon either plans ahead or anticipates outcomes (but not both), then he is strategic.
axiom(s3,rule([xor(plans_ahead(ramon),anticipates_outcomes(ramon))],strategic(ramon))).

% Anyone who analyzes situations or evaluates risks can solve problems logically.
axiom(s4,rule([or(analyzes_situations(X),evaluates_risks(X))],solves_problems_logically(X))).

% Ramon is fascinated by tactics.
axiom(s5,fascinated_by_tactics(ramon)).

% If Ramon is strategic, then he is either creative or a logical problem solver, but not both.
axiom(s6,rule([strategic(ramon)],xor(creative(ramon),logical_problem_solver(ramon)))).

% Ramon does not evaluate risks.
axiom(s7,not(evaluates_risks(ramon))).

% Ramon plans ahead.
axiom(s8,plans_ahead(ramon)).

% Ramon plays chess.
axiom(s9,plays_chess(ramon)).

% Anyone who sets goals or makes plans is strategic.
axiom(s10,rule([or(sets_goals(X),makes_plans(X))],strategic(X))).

% If someone is fascinated by tactics, then they study games and learn from experience.
axiom(s11,rule([fascinated_by_tactics(X)],and(studies_games(X),learns_from_experience(X)))).
